title: Imposter Syndrome: Why You Feel Like a Fraud (And How to Overcome It)

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们除了用时间换取金钱之外还能赚取其他收入，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特（Marianne Trent）博士，一名临床心理学家，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动收入和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个激动人心的好消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特（Sophie Foote）的“一对多”项目现在已经开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我在2022年亲自参加了这个项目，此后也一直支持两批心理学家走过他们的成长历程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的额外福利以及我提供的专属支持套餐，且无需支付额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四场小组大师班、大师课、个性化指导、一份福特南·梅森（Fortnum and Mason）的礼品，以及限时的一对一教练辅导福利。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过简介中链接的我的福利页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得这些福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在这里。

sentences.en: Have you ever felt that you're not good enough despite all of your achievements?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾觉得，尽管取得了种种成就，但自己还是不够优秀？

sentences.en: Like any moment, someone might find you out and realise you don't belong.
sentences.zh: 就像随时都可能有人把你看穿，意识到你不属于这里一样。

sentences.en: That is imposter syndrome and it affects even the most successful people.
sentences.zh: 这就是冒名顶替综合征，它甚至会影响最成功的人。

sentences.en: In today's episode, I'll break down exactly why this happens, how it can undermine your confidence, and most importantly, how you can stop it from holding you back.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我将详细剖析这种现象发生的原因、它如何削弱你的自信，以及最重要的是，你如何阻止它阻碍你的发展。

sentences.en: Whether you're starting a new career or just feeling the pressure to be perfect, imposter syndrome can creep in.
sentences.zh: 无论你是在开启一段新职业，还是仅仅感受着追求完美的压力，冒名顶替综合征都可能悄然侵袭。

sentences.en: But here's the truth.
sentences.zh: 但事实是这样的。

sentences.en: You do belong.
sentences.zh: 你的确属于这里。

sentences.en: And today we're going to talk about why.
sentences.zh: 今天我们将探讨其中的原因。

sentences.en: Stick around for some practical strategies which will help you change the way you think about yourself for good.
sentences.zh: 请留下来听听一些实用的策略，它们将彻底帮助你改变对自己的看法。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听《有抱负的心理学家播客》（The Aspiring Psychologist Podcast）。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne and I am a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安博士，我是一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Now, you might be like, well, of course, she doesn't have imposter syndrome, what with being qualified and all.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会想：“好吧，当然了，她怎么会有冒名顶替综合征，毕竟她是有资质的专业人士嘛。”

sentences.en: But this does happen for people in all walks of life and all stages of their career.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况确实会发生在各行各业以及职业各个阶段的人身上。

sentences.en: And I can assure you, it does crop up for me from time to time.
sentences.zh: 我可以向你保证，它确实不时会在我身上出现。

sentences.en: And people across all ages and backgrounds and job roles can experience it.
sentences.zh: 各个年龄段、不同背景和工作岗位的人都会经历这种感受。

sentences.en: And it can be really debilitating.
sentences.zh: 而且它真的会让人备受打击。

sentences.en: It can, of course, affect mental health, career growth, and personal development.
sentences.zh: 它当然会影响心理健康、职业发展和个人成长。

sentences.en: And let's get to grips with it so that you can take control of it rather than vice versa.
sentences.zh: 让我们来弄清它的本质，这样你就能掌控它，而不是让它掌控你。

sentences.en: So what exactly is imposter syndrome?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟什么是冒名顶替综合征？

sentences.en: Well, it's like an internal sense that you are not enough or that somehow all of the things you've achieved are not actually down to you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就像是一种内在的感觉，觉得自己做得不够好，或者不知为何，你取得的所有成就其实都不是你自己的功劳。

sentences.en: It's down to luck or chance or someone's done you a favour and you haven't earned what you've achieved or you don't deserve to be there.
sentences.zh: 而是归功于运气或机遇，或者别人帮了你一把，你并没有赢得你所取得的成就，也不配待在那里。

sentences.en: It might be that awareness that others are way more qualified or more appropriate to kind of speak or be doing what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 你可能会意识到，其他人比你更有资格，或者更适合发表言论或做你正在做的事。

sentences.en: It's basically like a real focus on everything you've got being down to external factors.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是极度关注你所拥有的一切，并将其归咎于外部因素。

sentences.en: So things that are not internal, not within your control.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些内在的、不受你控制的因素之外的东西。

sentences.en: And that can leave us feeling quite diminished and quite small.
sentences.zh: 这会让我们感到自己的价值大打折扣，觉得自己很渺小。

sentences.en: And kind of, of course, if we feel that way, it makes sense that we think that we shouldn't be there.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果我们有这种感觉，那么我们认为自己不应该待在那里也就合情合理了。

sentences.en: And whatever your job role, perhaps you're working in mental health, perhaps you're working in the psychology field, or perhaps you're doing something completely unrelated.
sentences.zh: 无论你的工作岗位是什么，也许你在心理健康领域工作，也许你在心理学领域工作，或者你从事着完全不相关的工作。

sentences.en: If you kind of find yourself being praised for something or you're being put forward for a new role, or perhaps even you've got a new role, you've got a promotion,
sentences.zh: 如果你发现自己因为某事而受到表扬，或者被推荐担任新职务，甚至也许你已经担任了新职务、得到了晋升，

sentences.en: this can be really common times that that sense of imposter syndrome come in.
sentences.zh: 这些往往都是冒名顶替综合征感悄然袭来的非常普遍的时期。

sentences.en: If you are working in academia, perhaps you've got a book coming out or you've published an important paper, and it can kind of strike you at key moments like that.
sentences.zh: 如果你在学术界工作，也许你有一本书要出版，或者你发表了一篇重要的论文，它就可能会在这样关键的时刻突然击中你。

sentences.en: So why does it happen?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么会发生这种事呢？

sentences.en: Well, firstly, it happens because we're human.
sentences.zh: 首先，发生这种事是因为我们是人。

sentences.en: We've got an awareness of ourselves and where we fit in society, in culture, in our families, in our social circles, in our workplaces.
sentences.zh: 我们对自我以及我们在社会、文化、家庭、社交圈和工作场所中的定位有着认知。

sentences.en: And we've got an awareness of where others fit as well.
sentences.zh: 我们对别人的定位也有所认知。

sentences.en: We can create judgments about ourselves, but we can also create judgments and have opinions of others.
sentences.zh: 我们既能对自己做出判断，也能对他人做出判断并持有看法。

sentences.en: Of course, whether we've had experiences in the past where we've been treated nicely, kindly, considerately, compassionately, can also impact on how our self-worth has developed.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在过去是否经历过被善待、友善、体贴、富有同情心的对待，也会影响我们自我价值感的建立。

sentences.en: Perfectionism, fear of failure, and high expectations, either from yourself and or others, can all fuel feelings of inadequacy, of not being enough.
sentences.zh: 完美主义、对失败的恐惧，以及来自你自己或他人的高期望，都会加剧能力不足感，觉得“自己还不够好”。

sentences.en: And if, when you were young, you were constantly compared to siblings or others in your class,
sentences.zh: 如果在你小时候，你总是被拿来与兄弟姐妹或班上的其他人作比较，

sentences.en: or humiliated for not knowing certain things, or not being good enough, or others being better, you might find that that perhaps creeps in more as a sense of imposter syndrome,
sentences.zh: 或者因为不知道某些事情、不够优秀或不如别人好而受到羞辱，你可能会发现，当事情对你更有利时，

sentences.en: when things are going better for you.
sentences.zh: 这种冒名顶替的感觉可能会更多地悄然浮现。

sentences.en: Or when you do have kind of the trappings of things going well, like a higher salary,
sentences.zh: 或者，当你确实拥有了事情进展顺利的象征时，比如更高的薪水，

sentences.en: or, I don't know, perhaps a nice car, or a home that feels comfortable and safe and within your control, it can make you feel, well, who am I to have these things?
sentences.zh: 或者，我不知道，也许是一辆不错的车，或者一个感觉舒适安全且在你的掌控之中的家，它会让你觉得：“好吧，我算什么身份能拥有这些东西呢？”

sentences.en: Because I'm just that kid, you know, did X, Y, and Z and wasn't enough.
sentences.zh: 因为我只是那个曾经做过这样那样的事情、却还不够优秀的孩子。

sentences.en: And, you know, people were laughing at, or my parents didn't even think I was good enough.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，别人都在嘲笑我，或者我的父母甚至认为我不够优秀。

sentences.en: And so, if you're getting that feedback that actually you are credible, or you are worthwhile, you are worth listening to,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你得到的反馈实际上是你值得信赖、很有价值、值得被倾听，

sentences.en: that can tap into the earlier roots that make you perhaps feel that you're not.
sentences.zh: 这可能会触及那些让你觉得自己不行的早期根源。

sentences.en: And, of course, there's cultural and societal influences as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中还有文化和社会的影响。

sentences.en: So, your gender may come into play here.
sentences.zh: 因此，你的性别可能会在这里发挥作用。

sentences.en: You know, is it safe for women to achieve?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，女性取得成就是安全的吗？

sentences.en: Is it safe for men to achieve?
sentences.zh: 男性取得成就是安全的吗？

sentences.en: Is it safe for people of different ethnicities, different backgrounds, to be in the role that you are in, or to be striving for the role that you are in?
sentences.zh: 不同种族、不同背景的人处于你目前的角色中，或者为争取你目前的角色而奋斗，是安全的吗？

sentences.en: If people are vocal, saying that people of your background, your upbringing, your wealth, your class,
sentences.zh: 如果有人直言不讳地指出，具有你这种背景、成长经历、财富状况、阶层的人，

sentences.en: should or should not be in particular areas, it can leave a little bit of an Achilles heel, a little bit of a weakness that kind of can get in on a bad day,
sentences.zh: 本该或不该处于某些特定领域，这就会留下一处阿喀琉斯之踵，一个微小的软肋，它会在你状态不佳的日子里乘虚而入，

sentences.en: on a day where you're feeling at a low ebb, and really give a chance for that imposter syndrome to ramp up and make you feel like you're not enough.
sentences.zh: 在你情绪低落的日子里，给冒名顶替综合征提供一个卷土重来的机会，让你觉得自己远远不够优秀。

sentences.en: So, what are the common signs of imposter syndrome?
sentences.zh: 那么，冒名顶替综合征的常见迹象有哪些？

sentences.en: And how might you notice if you are experiencing it?
sentences.zh: 你如何能察觉到自己是否正在经历它？

sentences.en: So, this is where the self-doubt and the negative self-talk might creep in.
sentences.zh: 这就是自我怀疑和消极的自我对话可能悄然潜入的地方。

sentences.en: It can be really helpful to just tune in to your inner voice.
sentences.zh: 倾听你内心的声音会非常有帮助。

sentences.en: And just imagine if this was someone in your team, or in your family, or in your friendship circle, whether you would consider them to be a positive person,
sentences.zh: 试着想象一下，如果这是你团队中的某个人、你家庭中的某个人，或者是你朋友圈里的某个人，你会认为他们是一个积极的人吗，

sentences.en: or whether you think they might be somebody who tends to put you down and not always be that nice.
sentences.zh: 还是会觉得他们是一个往往会贬低你、并不总是那么友善的人？

sentences.en: And if you think about carrying them around with you all the time on your shoulder or in your head, is that someone that is actually on your side?
sentences.zh: 如果你想象把这样一个人一直带在身边，扛在肩膀上或装在脑子里，这真的是一个站在你这边的人吗？

sentences.en: Or is it someone that's making you feel bad about yourself and all the situations that you might find yourself in
sentences.zh: 还是一个让你对自我以及你在日常生活中、在每周、每月、每年的各个时刻所陷入的所有处境感到糟糕的人？

sentences.en: throughout the day, throughout the week, throughout the month, throughout the year?
sentences.zh: 在日常生活中、在每周、每月、每年的各个时刻所陷入的所有处境感到糟糕的人？

sentences.en: Of course, what we know is imposter syndrome is not just linked or limited to our work, our education settings.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们所知道的是，冒名顶替综合征并不只与我们的工作或教育环境挂钩或受其局限。

sentences.en: It can crop up in friendship circles.
sentences.zh: 它也可能出现在朋友圈里。

sentences.en: It can crop up in family circles.
sentences.zh: 它也可能出现在家庭圈子里。

sentences.en: If you're a parent, it can crop up there, believe me, making you think, oh, wow, how am I old enough or experienced enough to be the one that has to know the answers for this?
sentences.zh: 如果你是个父母，它也会出现在那里，相信我，它会让你觉得：“哦，天哪，我怎么足够成熟或富有经验，来当那个必须知道这一切答案的人呢？”

sentences.en: I was in London recently with my children, one in each hand as we were navigating our way through the tube.
sentences.zh: 我最近带着孩子们在伦敦，我们穿梭于地铁站时，我一手牵着一个。

sentences.en: And it just kind of made me, I had this moment of, oh, how, how is this my job?
sentences.zh: 这让我不禁有了一种这样的时刻：“哦，怎么会，这怎么成了我的工作？”

sentences.en: How am I the one that's in charge?
sentences.zh: 怎么我成了那个负责任的人？

sentences.en: How am I the one that is looking at all the kind of tube maps and working out where to go?
sentences.zh: 怎么我成了那个看着各种地铁图并计算该去哪里的人？

sentences.en: There's surely someone that is far more experienced and far more capable and maybe more fun as a parent than me for doing this.
sentences.zh: 肯定有比我更有经验、更有能力，作为父母可能也比我更有趣的人来做这件事。

sentences.en: So it doesn't just crop up for our professional lives.
sentences.zh: 所以，它不仅仅会在我们的职业生活中冒出来。

sentences.en: You might find that you're undervaluing your achievements.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现自己在低估自己的成就。

sentences.en: So if you've done something cool or big or new, like a presentation or got a new job offer,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你做了一件很酷、很宏大或很新鲜的事，比如做了一次演讲或获得了新的工作邀约，

sentences.en: or maybe even just, you know, smashed your trip out of the park, taking your kids to London, you know, you might undervalue those accomplishments.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至只是，你知道的，把带着孩子去伦敦旅行这件事完成得极其出色，你都有可能会低估这些成就。

sentences.en: You might be like, well, you know, anyone could have done it or there weren't enough people applying for that job
sentences.zh: 你可能会想：“好吧，你知道的，任何人都能做到这一点”，或者“申请那份工作的人不够多”，

sentences.en: and said there was, you know, fewer people to pick from or, you know, it wasn't a real test because the trains all ran on time.
sentences.zh: 并说“你知道的，挑选的人更少了”，或者“你知道的，这根本算不上真正的考验，因为所有火车都准点运行”。

sentences.en: You know, there might be things that you were using to undervalue the fact that you did really well and you held it together and you, you know, you had a good result.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可能会用各种借口来贬低这样一个事实：你其实做得很好，你把一切都处理得井井有条，而且你知道的，你得到了一个好结果。

sentences.en: Another sign of imposter syndrome might be that sense that you are a fraud.
sentences.zh: 冒名顶替综合征的另一个迹象可能是觉得自己是个骗子。

sentences.en: You should not be doing what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 你不应该做你正在做的事。

sentences.en: It's just luck that you are.
sentences.zh: 你只是运气好才做到的。

sentences.en: Maybe you feel like people can see it on you.
sentences.zh: 也许你觉得别人能从你身上看出来。

sentences.en: You know, perhaps your skin feels marked and people are talking about you behind your back.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，也许你觉得自己的皮肤有瑕疵，别人正在背后议论你。

sentences.en: There can be a little bit of paranoia creeping in there as well.
sentences.zh: 这里也可能会滋生一点偏执情绪。

sentences.en: Of course, what we know about people that rise up through the ranks is that sometimes people will have things to say about you.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们对那些在职场步步高升的人的了解是，有时人们会对你评头论足。

sentences.en: They might well be saying some of these things, but it doesn't make it true.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能确实在说其中某些话，但这并不意味着它是真的。

sentences.en: If you've got evidence of your success, there has to be a time and a point and a place where you begin to lean on those,
sentences.zh: 如果你有自己成功的证据，总会有一个时间和地点，让你开始依靠这些证据，

sentences.en: where you begin to believe, connect and kind of hold those achievements, those successes,
sentences.zh: 让你开始相信、连结并把握住那些成就、那些成功，

sentences.en: that is, put them under your belt, use them as scaffolding to help you know, to help you feel that you do belong, that you have earned your stripes.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，把它们记在功劳簿上，把它们当作脚手架，来帮助你知道、帮助你觉得自己确实属于这里，你的付出实至名归。

sentences.en: Another sign of imposter syndrome might be over-preparation or perhaps what we call procrastination,
sentences.zh: 冒名顶替综合征的另一个迹象可能是过度准备，或者我们所说的拖延症，

sentences.en: kind of doing everything apart from the thing that is going to move your project across the line or get it to a point where it could come to reality.
sentences.zh: 也就是去做除了能让你的项目跨越终点线或使其成为现实之外的所有事情。

sentences.en: That can be a little bit like getting in our own way or not wanting to do the thing, prepare the thing for fear of judgment or for fear of it not being good enough,
sentences.zh: 这有点像是在给我们自己制造阻碍，或者因为害怕遭到评判、害怕不够优秀而不愿去做这件事、去准备这件事，

sentences.en: for fear of that being then open to ridicule or public comment.
sentences.zh: 因为害怕因此而招致嘲笑或公众的评头论足。

sentences.en: So now we have noticed the symptoms, the signs of imposter syndrome.
sentences.zh: 现在我们已经注意到了冒名顶替综合征的症状和迹象。

sentences.en: What are we going to do about it so that we can take control and have it be shrunk down to a more manageable size?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何应对，才能掌控它并将其缩小到更容易掌控的规模呢？

sentences.en: Firstly, we're going to acknowledge and reframe our thoughts and our thinking.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们要承认并重新构建我们的想法和思维方式。

sentences.en: We're just going to notice when those thoughts crop up initially.
sentences.zh: 当这些想法最初出现时，我们只需注意它们即可。

sentences.en: We might find it helpful to note them down just to kind of get a little bit of an overview over the days or the weeks of what kind of thoughts and feelings crop up.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会发现把它们记下来很有帮助，这样就能对几天或几周内浮现出的各种想法和感受有一个大致的了解。

sentences.en: We're then going to encourage a reframe of them.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们要鼓励自己重新审视它们。

sentences.en: Try to imagine what, you know, your best friend or someone close to you might say to help you feel differently about them.
sentences.zh: 试着想象一下，你知道的，你最好的朋友或亲近的人会说些什么来帮助你对它们产生不同的看法。

sentences.en: If you have a feeling that something is happening or should be happening or shouldn't be happening, we're going to try and turn down the volume on that a little bit.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一种感觉，觉得某事正在发生、应该发生或不应该发生，我们将试着把这种声音调小一点。

sentences.en: And we're going to try to look for more reliable, predictable external factors.
sentences.zh: 我们将试着寻找更可靠、可预测的外部因素。

sentences.en: We're going to look at facts, not feelings, because facts are more measurable.
sentences.zh: 我们要看事实，而不是感觉，因为事实更具可衡量性。

sentences.en: We're also going to be encouraging you to talk about this, to talk about this with your friends,
sentences.zh: 我们还鼓励你谈论这件事，与你的朋友谈论这件事，

sentences.en: to talk about this with your supervisors, to give it some oxygen, to give it some air.
sentences.zh: 与你的主管谈论这件事，给它一些氧气，让它见见空气。

sentences.en: Because what we know is that things that kind of hide in the damp, in the dark, can have a tendency to breed, to become bigger.
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道，那些藏在潮湿黑暗中的东西，往往会滋生并变得更大。

sentences.en: Because when we take control and we talk about them, it absolutely can help them to diminish, to shrink, and for you to be in control
sentences.zh: 因为当我们掌控它们并谈论它们时，绝对可以帮助它们减弱、缩小，从而让你重获掌控权，

sentences.en: and to kind of have all the evidence you need to feel like this is not true, that you do belong, that you do deserve to be there, and you can do what you're striving to do.
sentences.zh: 并且掌握你需要的所有证据，让你觉得这不是真的，你的确属于这里，你的确配得上待在那里，而且你能做到你正在努力去做的事情。

sentences.en: I absolutely hope and think that when you do give that the airtime, that you need to, to honour yourself.
sentences.zh: 我绝对希望并相信，当你真正给予它所需的空气时间来尊重自己时，

sentences.en: You will be getting the message of just how common imposter syndrome is.
sentences.zh: 你就会明白冒名顶替综合征是多么普遍。

sentences.en: Other people will drop in examples of their own and validate and normalise your experiences, which can be so important.
sentences.zh: 其他人会分享他们自己的例子，并验证和正常化你的经历，这会非常重要。

sentences.en: Another way of kind of grappling with this and overcoming it is that we're going to begin to celebrate our successes, no matter how small.
sentences.zh: 应对和克服这一问题的另一种方法是，我们要开始庆祝我们的成功，无论多小。

sentences.en: Even if you're really enjoying a dinner that you've cooked for your family or your friends, you're going to kind of say,
sentences.zh: 即使你真的很享受为家人或朋友烹制的晚餐，你也要说：

sentences.en: I really love this, like I think I've done a great job here.
sentences.zh: “我真的很喜欢这样，我觉得我在这里做得太棒了。”

sentences.en: It might feel really uncomfortable to begin with.
sentences.zh: 一开始可能会觉得很不自然。

sentences.en: But also if you've done a big thing, you know, if you have submitted a really important assignment or you've got a great mark back from something that you've put in
sentences.zh: 但同样，如果你做了一件大事，你知道的，如果你提交了一份非常重要的作业，或者从你投入的工作中得到了很高的分数，

sentences.en: or you've had a grant approved or, you know, you've got promotion or you've got an interview, we're going to celebrate those steps,
sentences.zh: 或者你获得了拨款批准，或者你知道的，你得到了晋升，或者你通过了一场面试，我们都要庆祝这些步骤，

sentences.en: no matter how small or inconsequential they might be because they are worth celebrating.
sentences.zh: 无论它们可能多么微小或不足挂齿，因为它们都值得庆祝。

sentences.en: They are markers of our success, of our progress through whatever life stage or career you find yourself in.
sentences.zh: 它们是我们成功的标志，是我们度过无论什么人生阶段或职业生涯的进步标志。

sentences.en: It isn't arrogant.
sentences.zh: 这并不傲慢。

sentences.en: It isn't braggy.
sentences.zh: 这也不是吹嘘。

sentences.en: It's really important that you begin to show up for yourself positively with compassion, with grace, with praise and admiration, not just criticism, shame and derision.
sentences.zh: 非常重要的是，你要开始以积极、富有同情心、优雅、赞赏和钦佩的态度来支持自己，而不仅仅是批评、羞耻和嘲弄。

sentences.en: And our last tip is that we're going to develop what's called a growth mindset.
sentences.zh: 我们的最后一条建议是，我们要培养所谓的“成长型思维”。

sentences.en: We're going to reduce perfectionism and we're going to allow what mistakes in and know that that's a really important learning journey and that that happens for a reason.
sentences.zh: 我们要减少完美主义，我们要允许犯错的发生，并知道这是一段非常重要的学习历程，而且犯错是有原因的。

sentences.en: We need to be able to learn from setbacks along the way and to talk about them and to reframe them and to own them as well.
sentences.zh: 我们需要能够从一路走来的挫折中吸取教训，谈论它们，重新构建它们，并勇于承担它们。

sentences.en: You know, we don't get to high stages of our career without making some mistakes along the way.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们在职业生涯中若不经历一些错误，是无法达到很高的高度。

sentences.en: That is normal.
sentences.zh: 这是正常的。

sentences.en: That is part of being human.
sentences.zh: 这是身为人类的一部分。

sentences.en: But of course, we need to learn from them too.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们也需要从中吸取教训。

sentences.en: I'm reminded where we were having a roof redone on our house and a trainee roofer fell through the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 我想起以前我们家在重新翻修屋顶时，一个见习修屋顶的工人从天花板上掉了下来。

sentences.en: And I was told it only happens once because we learn from our mistakes.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我，这种事只发生一次，因为我们从错误中吸取了教训。

sentences.en: We learn from that pain and we learn to kind of look and be more cautious about where we place our feet.
sentences.zh: 我们从那种痛苦中学习，并学会观察和更加谨慎地对待我们落脚的地方。

sentences.en: And whilst I hope you won't fall through a roof, the same is true from what you are doing in whatever job role you are into.
sentences.zh: 虽然我希望你不会从屋顶掉下来，但在你所从事的任何工作岗位上，你所做的事情也是同样的道理。

sentences.en: If you are experiencing imposter syndrome, please know you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在经历冒名顶替综合征，请知道你并不孤单。

sentences.en: It is super, super common.
sentences.zh: 这真的是超级超级普遍。

sentences.en: Everyone faces self-doubt at times, but that doesn't mean that you are not deserving of your successes.
sentences.zh: 每个人有时都会面临自我怀疑，但这并不意味着你不配拥有你的成功。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that you can't pass go, that you can't collect 200 pounds and go to the next stage of your career.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你不能过关，不能领取200英镑，并进入职业生涯的下一个阶段。

sentences.en: Little Monopoly reference there.
sentences.zh: 这里有个小小的“大富翁”梗。

sentences.en: As a little action point here, why don't you write down three things that you've done recently that you think have been good enough or that you're proud or pleased have happened.
sentences.zh: 作为行动指南，为什么不写下你最近做过三件你认为足够好、或者让你感到骄傲和高兴的事情呢？

sentences.en: Really reflect on what it's taken from you to achieve those things, to get them in the bag, to make them happen.
sentences.zh: 好好反思一下，为了实现这些目标、取得成功并将它们化为现实，你付出了怎样的努力。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for your time in tuning in today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家今天收听。

sentences.en: If you're watching on YouTube, please do subscribe, like, drop me a comment and share with anyone you think might find this useful too.
sentences.zh: 如果你在YouTube上观看，请务必订阅、点赞、留言，并分享给任何你觉得会有帮助的人。

sentences.en: Please do come and connect with me on my socials where I'm Dr. Marianne Trent Everywhere and join my free Facebook group,
sentences.zh: 欢迎在各大社交媒体上与我互动，我到处都是“玛丽安·特伦特博士”（Dr. Marianne Trent Everywhere），并加入我的免费Facebook群组：

sentences.en: The Aspiring Psychologist Community, which is the unique home of Marianne's motivation and mindset sessions.
sentences.zh: “有志心理学家社区”（The Aspiring Psychologist Community），这里是玛丽安的动力与心态分享的独特家园。

sentences.en: If it is your time and you're ready for the next step in progressing your psychology career, please also do consider checking out the Aspiring Psychologist membership,
sentences.zh: 如果时机成熟，你准备好在心理学职业生涯中迈出下一步，也请考虑了解“有志心理学家会员”（Aspiring Psychologist membership），

sentences.en: which you can join with no minimum term from just £30 a month.
sentences.zh: 你可以随时加入，无最低期限要求，每月仅需30英镑起。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for being part of my world.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们成为我世界的一部分。

sentences.en: I will look forward to bringing you the next episode on YouTube from 10am on Saturdays and wherever you get your podcasts from 6am on Mondays.
sentences.zh: 我期待着周六上午10点开始在YouTube上为您带来下一期节目，以及每周一上午6点在各大播客平台与您见面。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚取超越“出卖时间换金钱”的收入会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，我自2019年以来一直在开发被动和循环收入来源。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要宣布。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's one-to-many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，比如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于2022年完成了这个项目，此后也一直陪伴并支持了两届心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖品以及我提供的独家支持套餐，且无需额外付费。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 其中包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四场团体大师班、大师讲座、个性化指导、一份福南梅森（Fortnum and Mason）礼品，以及限时一对一教练指导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多详情。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。
